title: From Open Cholecystectomy to Laparoscopic Cholecystectomy: The University of Benin Teaching Hospital Experience
abstract:
The University of Benin Teaching Hospital (UBTH) general surgical laparoscopic surgery began
in November 2020. It is one of the few tertiary institutions persistently offering laparoscopic
services in south-south Nigeria. There has been remarkable increase in the number of
cholecystectomies via laparoscopy over the years compared to the preceding 5years of its
commencement. This study aimed to highlight the remarkable change in the uptake of
cholecystectomy in UBTH since the commencement of laparoscopic surgery. The records of
cholecystectomies done over 10 years were reviewed; 5-years prior to and 5-years post-
commencement of general surgery laparoscopy. All data obtained were analyzed using Excel.
keywords: Cholecystectomy, Open cholecystectomy, Laparoscopic cholecystectomy, South-South Nigeria.
affiliations:
Department of Surgery,1 University of Benin/University of
Benin Teaching Hospital, Benin City, Nigeria

title: Comparison of Early Versus Delayed Enteral Feeding in Adult Patients with Uncomplicated Appendicitis Following Open Appendicectomy in University of Benin Teaching Hospital, Benin City
authors: Ediale MO<sup>1</sup>, Agbonrofo PI<sup>1,2</sup>, Odigie VI<sup>1,2</sup>, Nwashilli NJ<sup>1</sup>
abstract:
Open Appendicectomy is one of the most common general surgical emergency procedures that requires a period of hospital stay. Conventionally, enteral feeding commences after the passage of flatus or faeces or normoactive bowel sounds. Delayed bowel motions may result in prolonged postoperative recovery. This study aimed to determine the difference in outcome between early and delayed enteral feeding post-appendicectomy in University of Benin Teaching Hospital. This was a 12-month prospective, observational, randomized, 
comparative study. All adult patients who met the inclusion criteria were recruited and randomized, equally,
into Groups A and B. Early enteral feeding commenced six hours post open appendicectomy and delayed
enteral feeding commenced after the passage of flatus or faeces.
keywords: Acute appendicitis, Appendicectomy, Early enteral feeding, Delayed enteral feeding
affiliations:

Hospital, Benin City, Nigeria. Department of Surgery,2
University of Benin, Benin City, Nigeria

title: Primary Male Urethral Adenocarcinoma: Case Report and Review of Literature
authors: Akaiso OE<sup>1*</sup>, Ukpong AE<sup>1</sup>, Udoh EA<sup>1</sup>
abstract:
Primary Adenocarcinoma of the male urethra is a rare tumour accounting for less than 1% of
malignancies worldwide. It is highly aggressive and causes malignant urethral obstruction. The aim of this case report was to highlight its rarity and misdiagnosis as urethral stricture, due to similarities in presentation. The patient’s clinical presentation, investigations and treatment were retrospectively extracted from his case note. A 54 year old male patient with two-year history of lower urinary tract symptoms and acute urinary retention presented in the urology clinic.
keywords: Urethral cancer, stricture, primary urethral adenocarcinoma

Urology Division,1 Department of Surgery, University of
Uyo, Uyo

title: Prevalence, Aetiology and Outcomes of Antepartum Haemorrhage at Nnamdi Azikiwe University Teaching Hospital, Nnewi, Nigeria
authors: Ezeigwe CO1,2, Emegokor AI1,2, Igwilo KC1,2, Obi KE1,2, Ogelle OM1,2, Okudo J3, Alabi OO4,5, Olorunfemi G1,6
abstract: Antepartum haemorrhage (APH) defined as bleeding from the genital tract after the age of viability which remains 28 weeks is a common obstetric emergency with associated perinatal and maternal morbidity and mortality in Nigeria. This study assessed the prevalence, aetiology and foeto-maternal outcomes of pregnancies complicated by APH in Nnamdi Azikiwe University Teaching Hospital, Nnewi. This study was a 5-year retrospective cross-sectional study. A proforma was used to retrieve the sociodemographic characteristics, causes and risk factors for APH, maternal outcome and foetal outcomes from patients’ medical records from 1st January 2019 to 31st December 2023.
keywords: Antepartum Haemorrhage, Maternal death, Maternal morbidity

title: Urethral Stricture Disease: Aetiology, Clinical Presentation and Management in University of Uyo Teaching Hospital, Nigeria
authors: Akaiso OE1,2*, Ukpong AE1,2, Udoh EA1,2
abstract: Urethral stricture defined as a narrowing of the urethra consequent upon ischaemic  pongiofibrosis is a relatively common urological problem in adult males and leads to lower urinary tract obstruction. This study was aimed to report on the aetiology, clinical presentation and management of anterior urethral strictures. This was a retrospective study carried out between January 2012 and December 2022, of male patients with urethral strictures treated at University of Uyo Teaching Hospital. Data obtained included age, occupation, etiology of the strictures, clinical features, investigations, treatment and outcome. A total of 49 male patients were included. The age range was 3-75 years (mean= 35.67).

title: Diagnostic Accuracy of Cytological Grading and Histopathological Diagnosis of Breast Lesions - A 4 Year Retrospective Study
authors: Richard SK1*, Kwaghe BV2, Emeribe NA3, Awosusi BL4
abstract: Breast lump is commonest presenting complaint seen at the surgical breast clinic. Breast cancer is the commonest malignancy of women globally and accurate diagnosis in specialized centres depends on the combined findings from clinical examination, radiological analysis, cytology and histopathological evaluations of biopsied breast lesions. This study aimed to correlate cytological grading and histopathological diagnosis obtained after the evaluation of breast lesions. This is a retrospective study of 52 included cases that were seen at the general surgical clinic that met the inclusion criteria. Cytological grades and histopathological grades were obtained from their records. cytological and histopathological slides were retrieved and reassessed by two independent pathologists.
keywords: Cytology, Histology, Breast lump, Breast cancer.

title: Steroid Induced Ocular Hypertension and Treatment in A 40 Year General Medical Practitioner.
abstract:
Steroids are used in clinical practice to treat a wide range of disease conditions and in
ophthalmic practice in treating both extraocular and especially intraocular inflammatory
processes because of the need to prevent undesirable effects of inflammation in the eye.
1,2 Duke elder et al 3 were the first in a series of cases to document its use in treating various
ocular disease conditions. However, they were discovered to have ocular side effects such as
cataract and steroid induced ocular hypertension (SIOH) and eventual glaucoma that could compromise vision.4
keywords: Antiglaucoma, Conjunctivitis, Glaucoma, Ocular hypertension, Steroid, Visual loss.
affiliations:

title: Prevalence and Pattern of Ocular Manifestations of HIV/AIDS among Adult Patients on Highly Active Anti-Retroviral Therapy in Federal Medical Centre Lokoja, Nigeria
authors: Oseji DI1, Odi AF1, Monsudi KF2*, Mahmoud AO3, Onah ES4
abstract: Acquired immunodeficiency syndrome (AIDS) is a group of health problems characterized by severe reduction or loss of the body’s cellular immunity, which adversely affects the resistance to infection and malignancy.1-3 It is caused by acquired immunodeficiency virus (HIV). AIDS was first described clinically in 1981 when five cases of pneumocystis carinii causing pneumocystis pneumonia were reported in previously healthy young men, and since then it has been a pandemic especially in sub-Saharan Africa.

title: Evaluation of Serum Magnesium, Calcium, Phosphate and Antioxidant Vitamins in Sickle Cell Patients in Kano State-Nigeria
authors: Ahmad MB<sup>1</sup>, Yusuf H<sup>2</sup> and Madaki S<sup>1</sup>
abstract: Sickle cell disease (SCD) is a severe genetic disorder, particularly prevalent in sub-Saharan Africa, caused by a mutation in the β- globin gene leading to abnormal haemoglobinS (HbS). This results in red blood cells assuming a sickle shape under low oxygen conditions, causing vessel blockages. it leads to complications such as vaso-occlusive crises, chronic haemolytic anaemia, and tissue damage, posing a significant public health challenge.
